transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 10:00 PDT | 40 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (AcmePay Head of ML), Maya (Platform), Liam (CTO)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this short — quick sync on the caching POC, where we are at, hit rates, and next steps.
00:08 Carlos: Yep, thanks. Quick housekeeping, we were running the week-two tests against the hosted endpoint and our current observed KV hit rate is around 18% overall, and about 22% for small prompts. Those numbers are from last Friday's run.
00:23 Priya: Right, and to confirm, the measurement used exact string-match on the prompt prefix to determine hits? Or hash-based keying?
00:30 Carlos: It's the naive approach right now, we just used the full prompt text as the key, so it's pretty brittle.
00:36 Priya: OK that explains a lot. Exact-match will under-count if your prompts have any variability — spacing, user metadata, timestamps. We recommended canonicalization and a prompt-hash approach in the doc we shared — did you get that? (link posted: https://redwood.ai/sales/acmepay/cache-guidelines)
00:52 Carlos: We saw it, yeah. We're also concerned about collisions and privacy when hashing.
00:57 Jordan: Totally. For privacy we recommend a keyed HMAC with customer KMS, and we can truncate. For collisions, a 256-bit hash is effectively collision-free for your scale.
01:10 Liam: Quick question on TTLs — what's the recommendation? Right now it's set to 1 hour and our traffic has a lot of short-lived prompts.
01:16 Priya: For our workloads we usually do a tiered TTL: short prefix matches use 5-30 minutes, longer canonical prompts can be 2-6 hours. Also consider recompute vs stale-while-revalidate if you need low latency.
01:30 Carlos: Got it. If we tighten TTLs we might lose long-tail hits though. Our distribution is heavy tail; 80% of requests are 20% of prompts.
01:39 Priya: Exactly — that's the 80/20 you mentioned. We should focus on the top 20% canonical prompts for caching. Also, batching can improve cost, but it can lower cache hit rates if you change request grouping.
01:52 Jordan: On that point, last week's benchmark used batch size 8 on GPUs; we saw average latency drop but hit rate also dropped slightly because the system merged token streams and caused prefix mismatch in some edge cases.
02:05 Maya: Hmm, is that the runtime merging behavior? That could impact application-level expectations for per-request latency.
02:11 Priya: It's more about how we canonicalize requests before batching. If you include ephemeral metadata in the key, batching groups will not share the cache. So we want the key to be stable across batched requests.
02:25 Carlos: One of our blockers is that our prompt templates include user name and session id in the prefix. We're iterating to move that after the canonical prompt so it's not in the key.
02:34 Jordan: Great. That change alone should boost hit rates significantly. We saw similar in another customer where removing session IDs bumped KV hits from ~15% to ~40% for templated flows.
02:45 Liam: Okay curious about the economics — what kind of cost delta can we expect if we get from 18% to 45% hits?
02:52 Priya: Ballpark: depends on token distribution, but for your workload we estimate about 12-18% monthly token cost reduction if you hit 40-50% effective reuse on prefixes. We'll send a more detailed cost model after we get the exact sample prompt set.
03:05 Carlos: We'll share that prompt sample today.
03:08 Priya: Awesome. On the tech side, two immediate tuning levers: change key derivation (hash canonicalized prefix), and tune TTL/LRU policy. We'll run a controlled benchmark with those changes.
03:20 Jordan: Proposed experiment: we run three benchmark variants — (A) current baseline, (B) canonicalization + HMAC keying + TTL 30m, (C) same as B but TTL 60m and slightly more aggressive LRU. We'll capture KV hit, P50/P95 latency, and cost per 1M tokens.
03:39 Carlos: That sounds good. How long is each run?
03:42 Priya: 30 minutes each should be enough to see steady-state for your traffic mix; we can do them back-to-back with identical input streams.
03:50 Maya: Can you run those on a dedicated pool? We want to avoid noisy neighbors affecting latency numbers.
03:55 Jordan: For initial runs we can use hosted but with pinned instances; for the canary we recommended running on a dedicated pool to validate production latency — we suggested a 60-minute canary on dedicated on 2026-07-28.
04:08 Liam: What's the operational lift for dedicated? Network/VPC peering, security approvals — that could take a week or so.
04:15 Jordan: Understood. We can start with hosted (fast), then move to dedicated once we see positive delta. We'll also send the dedicated run playbook to your infra team (networking checklist, firewall rules, routing).
04:26 Maya: Please include SAML/KMS notes; our security team will want to confirm key management for the HMAC suggestion.
04:32 Priya: Will do — we'll include KMS integration options, we support customer-managed keys and an HSM workflow for signing.
04:40 Carlos: Any concerns about model quality when reusing prefixes? Are we risking stale or spurious outputs?
04:46 Priya: Good question. We will only cache final token sequences for identical prompts. For outputs that are non-deterministic or depend on recent state, we'll avoid caching or use shorter TTLs. Also we recommend quality checks: sample A/B between cached and fresh responses for your top prompts to validate parity.
05:05 Jordan: We'll provide a small eval harness and script to do periodic regression checks and record LLM metric differences.
05:11 Carlos: Great. Also curious — do you support partial KV cache hits (prefix present but continuation differs)?
05:16 Priya: Yes, the runtime supports prefix KV cache reuse for autoregressive decoders — but your keying must align with the decoder's prefix. If you canonicalize correctly we can reuse KV up to the matched prefix length and then generate remaining tokens. That usually gives good latency gains.
05:33 Jordan: Small note — sometimes the transcript says "KV cash" in our notes, just a small transcription quirk.
05:38 Carlos: (laughs) we've seen that.
05:40 Priya: Okay next steps recap: Priya will run the three benchmark variants and post results; Jordan will send cost delta and canary playbook; Carlos/Maya will share prompt dump and infra contacts. We'll sync next week and schedule the dedicated canary for 2026-07-28 pending infra OK.
05:58 Liam: Sounds good. Anything else?
06:00 Carlos: No, thanks.
06:02 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links to results and the recommended cache key fn. Meeting end.

References shared during meeting: deck: https://redwood.ai/sales/acmepay/cache-benchmarks | guidelines doc: https://redwood.ai/sales/acmepay/cache-guidelines
